title: The VLA/ALMA Nascent Disk And Multiplicity (VANDAM) Survey of Orion Protostars. V. A Characterization of Protostellar Multiplicity
question: What are the multiplicity fractions, companion fractions, and companion separation distributions of protostars in the Orion and Perseus molecular clouds, and what do they imply for the formation and evolution of multiple systems?

what.value: HOPS catalog of Orion protostars (classifications, L_bol, T_bol)

evidence.quote: The sample of Orion protostars is drawn from the HOPS Survey (cite: fischer2010; stutz2013; furlan2016).

what.value: Perseus protostar sample and catalog of positions

evidence.quote: The sample of protostars in the Perseus molecular cloud was selected from (cite: enoch2009), but we also included additional protostars that were identified from the millimeter continuum (cite: looney2000) and Herschel observations of the region (cite: sadavoy2014).
For the protostars in Perseus, we make use of the previously generated catalog from (cite: tobin2016a), which used similar methods to derive protostar positions with an earlier version of CASA.

what.value: Separation distribution and multiplicity data for field solar-type stars

evidence.quote: We make use of the observed separation distribution from 24 to 10$^4$ au from (cite: raghavan2010), sampling the same range of separations for which we have detections.

Using the data from (cite: raghavan2010), we calculate the field star MFs and CFs for system separations of 20 to 10$^4$ au (0.28$\pm$0.02 and 0.32$\pm$0.02, respectively), 20 to 10$^3$ au (0.22$\pm$0.02 and 0.23$\pm$0.02), and 20 to 500 au (0.19$\pm$0.02 and 0.20$\pm$0.02).

what.value: HST 1.6 micron companion detections toward HOPS protostars

evidence.quote: There were a total of 274 HOPS protostars observed by both ALMA/VLA and HST at 1.6 $\mu$m (cite: kounkel2016).

what.value: ALMA 1.3 mm continuum image of NGC 2024 FIR-3

evidence.loc: Close Multiples Not Detected By Both ALMA and VLA
evidence.quote: Given the association with a bonafide protostar system, we include this detection in our multiplicity statistics with a separation of 1.46$''$ ($\sim$586 au) and show the ALMA 1.3 mm image from (cite: vanterwisga2020) and the VLA images in Figure 5.

recipe.goal: Measure source positions, flux densities, and sizes from continuum images
recipe.method: Fit elliptical Gaussians to detected sources in ALMA and VLA continuum images and merge the ALMA and VLA catalogs

recipe.goal: Estimate local YSO surface density around each protostar
recipe.method: Compute local YSO surface density using the 11th nearest neighbor distance in infrared YSO catalogs (corrected with X-ray catalogs in Orion), adding ALMA/VLA detections if no catalog source is within 2.5''
key_parameters: 11th nearest neighbor; 2.5'' matching radius; 30 pc^-2 boundary between high and low YSO density

recipe.method: Iterative inside-out nearest-neighbor search in 100 logarithmically spaced radial bins from 15 au to 10^4 au, replacing paired sources with their unweighted geometric midpoint
key_parameters: Search radius: 15 au to 10^4 au in 100 logarithmically spaced radial bins
assumptions: Spatial association in projected separation alone assigns multiplicity; unweighted geometric midpoint represents paired position

recipe.goal: Calculate companion probabilities and multiplicity/companion fractions (MF and CF)
recipe.method: Compute Bayesian probability P(companion|detection) using Poisson expectation of unassociated YSOs, iteratively updating P(companion) with CF until convergence; round sum of component probabilities to assign system order and compute MF and CF with Wilson score or Poisson uncertainties
key_parameters: P(detection|companion) = 0.75; probability cutoff = 0.001; 3 iterations for convergence (< 0.005 change); P(companion) = 0.14 (<500 au), 0.19 (<10^3 au), 0.46 (<10^4 au); z = 1.0 for Wilson interval; Poisson uncertainty for CF > 0.5
assumptions: Survey sensitivity of ~1 M_earth detects 75% of disk-bearing YSOs and protostellar companions

recipe.goal: Construct and statistically compare companion separation distributions and luminosity distributions
recipe.method: Generate separation histograms (bin size 0.25 in log10(au)) and probability-weighted CDFs; randomly sample CDFs 1000 times according to companion probabilities and perform one-sided or two-sided Kolmogorov-Smirnov (KS) tests
key_parameters: Histogram bin size = 0.25 dex; 1000 Monte Carlo CDF realizations; significance threshold p <= 0.01

answer_key.quantity: Submillimeter/centimeter companion detection incompleteness (100 to 10^3 au)

evidence.quote: Between $10^2$ and $10^3$ au, we estimate a submillimeter/centimeter incompleteness of $\sim$20% (as given by 1-[Number of detected companions/Total companions]; Total companions is the millimeter plus infrared companions). Considering only Class I and Flat Spectrum protostars, the incompleteness rises to 29%.

answer_key.quantity: Fraction of non-coeval multiple systems in Orion

evidence.quote: Of the multiple systems identified, 42% of Class 0 multiple systems have a non-coeval member compared to 22% of Class I systems, and just 4% of Flat Spectrum systems have a non-coeval member. In total, the number of systems with a non-coveal member is 25%, which is comparable to results from Perseus.

score_reason: The paper provides a remarkably detailed, step-by-step mathematical and algorithmic description of the catalog pairing, Bayesian contamination correction, and statistical testing in Section 2.4 and Appendix A, and hosts reduced continuum images on Harvard Dataverse as well as full machine-readable input catalogs. Minor deductions are due to custom analysis scripts not being released and calibration/imaging details being deferred to Paper I.
rediscovery_reason: All reduced continuum images are public on Harvard Dataverse, the complete input source catalogs (positions, classes, L_bol, T_bol, YSO surface densities, distances) are published as machine-readable tables, and the pairing/probability recipe is fully specified with extensive numeric answer keys (Tables 3-9).
